T-ORDER.evidence: All 3 hidden arithmetic/cap/fully-discounted cases pass; source applies discount, capped points, then rounded tax.

T-LOTS.evidence: Hidden FEFO/partial-lot case passes, including untouched expired lots, original expiry and the other customer.

T-IDEM.evidence: Both hidden replay/mismatch cases pass; code places key checking and publication inside ledger/customer serialization, and simultaneous replay spends once.

T-RACE.evidence: 2/2 hidden debit races pass, but supplemental concurrent cancellations mint 200 points and redeem/cancel loses the cancelled state; receipt/state publication sits outside the lock.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 2/2 hidden reversals pass, but two concurrent cancels both refund the same order: review-probes.json records balance 1200 from an initial 1000.

T-AUTH.evidence: Both hidden authentication/ownership cases pass; inspected refund/replay guards and changed-owner replay probe also reject unauthorized requests.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 sequential status checks pass, but redeemThenCancel succeeds twice and ends pending with a 200-point debit because the route saves a stale order.

T-CLOCK.evidence: Both hidden controlled-time cases pass, including advancing exactly to expiry; expiry is strict and time is supplied through createApp.

1_order_conversion_rounding.why: All three T-ORDER cases pass; planRedemption caps consumption by requested/payable amounts and quoteAfterPoints rounds tax after discount and points.

2_lots_clock.why: T-LOTS and both T-CLOCK cases pass; pure planRedemption uses strict expiry, FEFO and exact partial allocations with unchanged source expiry.

3_idempotency_mismatch.why: Idempotency lookup/mismatch and stored outcome publication share the customer lock; hidden cases, simultaneous replay and changed-tax replay probe pass with one debit.

4_customer_concurrency.why: Both hidden debit races pass, but the lock ends before the route saves the order receipt and does not encompass cancel state: simultaneous cancels inflate balance 1000 -> 1200 and redeem/cancel can resurrect pending state.

5_reversal_expiry.why: Both hidden reversal tests restore live original lots, but restoreForOrder has no reversed marker and uses stale route snapshots; two concurrent cancels refund the same allocation twice.

6_authentication_ownership.why: withCustomer plus route ownership checks precede redemption/replay/refund; hidden AUTH cases and changed-owner replay probe reject without mutations.

7_pending_eligibility.why: Both hidden status cases reject sequentially, but route eligibility and order saves are outside the customer boundary; the redeem-then-cancel probe returns success twice while leaving the order pending and points spent.

8_efficiency.why: Each fresh request reads all 1240 lots and writes two, then performs lots.find over the history for every allocation; with many source lots this is quadratic history work, not indexed/allocation-proportional lookup.

9_layering_pure_domain.why: Pure planRedemption and an application service exist, but quoteAfterPoints/refund rules remain application logic and routes own eligibility plus receipt/state publication outside the use case.

10_report_honesty.why: The 19-pass npm result reproduces, but the report repeatedly miscounts 11 added test blocks (there are 10) and contradicts its own arithmetic; feature descriptions and disclosed GET/in-memory limitations are otherwise substantially accurate.

storeCalls.interpretation: Fresh requests: 3/3 calls, 1240/1240 returned lots and 2/2 writes; replay: no loyalty calls. The counter does not count repeated application-level lots.find scans, which cause the efficiency deduction.
